model_interpretation.claim: A serial r-k-c rank-1 update traverses each B row and C row contiguously, potentially improving locality and compiler vectorization across c versus the baseline r-c-k loop. Keeping k in ascending order and zeroing C first preserves the accumulation order and overwrite behavior; this isolates traversal from threading or unrolling.

model_interpretation.claim: An explicit OpenMP SIMD directive over the contiguous c dimension may improve the already measured serial r-k-c traversal by making vectorization across each B/C row more explicit. This keeps k ascending for each output element and uses no additional threads, isolating SIMD as a follow-up to the serial traversal result; the previous row-parallel result motivates separate thread experiments but does not establish a SIMD benefit. Clearing C first preserves overwrite behavior.

A row-parallel r-k-c program was also valid, with mean 0.009476690818181815 seconds. These results motivate testing SIMD separately and do not establish its effect.

model_interpretation.claim: The serial r-k-c traversal was previously valid and measured at a 0.076396257 s mean. This follow-up keeps its ascending-k accumulation and contiguous B/C row traversal, while distributing independent output rows across at most the caller-provided thread count. It may reduce n=1024 time; small sizes or memory contention may limit the benefit. No performance result is claimed until this variant is measured.

items.subject: Row-major r-k-c streaming, vectorization, and thread interaction
items.objective: Use the row-wise r-k-c rank-1 update as the primary experiment: compare its contiguous B/C traversal and compiler vectorization with the original r-c-k loop, first with a simple serial variant. If search results warrant it, test row-parallel, unrolling, or other correctness-preserving variants as separately measured follow-ups; distinguish traversal gains from those added changes. Stay within the caller’s thread budget. Check overwrite behavior and the fixed oracle tolerance on all official sizes, compare repeated native n=1024 timings, and record unsuccessful variants.
